rows.passage_en: Periodic fire in fire-adapted ecosystems can consume accumulated dead vegetation and other fuel. Without such fires, fuel can build up and contribute to more severe later fires.
rows.review_note: NPS explicitly describes fuels accumulating after fire exclusion. This is ecosystem-dependent, not a blanket claim that every wildfire is beneficial.

rows.passage_en: Long loops of Henle extend deep into the renal medulla and contribute to the osmotic gradient needed to concentrate urine. Desert-adapted mammals such as kangaroo rats commonly have many long-loop nephrons.
rows.review_note: Indexed excerpt supports arid-adapted mammals; full article returned a browser challenge. Need accessible full primary physiology passage before final approval. Relationship is not a universal one-variable predictor.

rows.passage_en: Pure water in an open beaker has reference water potential zero. Dissolved solutes lower water potential; water moves into a cell whose total water potential is lower than that of its surroundings.
rows.review_note: AP manual explicitly describes cells initially negative before pressure rises. Fresh potato assumption is intended; fully turgid tissue equilibrated with pure water can have total potential zero. Review that unstated initial-state assumption before approval.

rows.passage_en: Robert MacArthur and Edward O. Wilson developed an equilibrium model of island biogeography and presented it in a 1963 article and a fuller 1967 book.
rows.review_note: Author Wilson directly recounts collaboration; no claim they were the first humans to study geographic species distributions.

rows.source_locator: The Origin and Evolution of Cells, endosymbiosis
rows.passage_en: The endosymbiotic explanation proposes that mitochondria and chloroplasts arose from bacteria that became persistent residents inside other cells.
rows.review_note: Exact relevant indexed passage read; full page blocked. Mitochondria and chloroplasts arose in distinct endosymbiotic events, not one event producing both.

rows.passage_en: The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to reduce fixed carbon into carbohydrates. During this use, ATP becomes ADP and NADPH is oxidized back to NADP+.
rows.review_note: Sugar shorthand includes exported triose phosphate and subsequent carbohydrate synthesis; not a claim free glucose is the immediate single-cycle product.

rows.source_locator: Innate Immunity, phagocytic cells in all animals
rows.passage_en: Invertebrate animals use innate immune defenses including phagocytic cells that engulf foreign material. Vertebrate-style B cells and helper or cytotoxic T lymphocytes are part of adaptive immunity.
rows.review_note: Indexed passage explicitly states invertebrate phagocytes and confines adaptive immunity to vertebrates in textbook terminology; full page blocked. Some invertebrate immune priming does not imply vertebrate B/T cells.

rows.passage_en: Lamarck’s historical account associated inherited change with the experiences and acquired changes of parents. Expecting acquired cold tolerance to pass to descendants resembles that account.
rows.review_note: This identifies a historical analogy, not scientific validation of Lysenko. Modern epigenetic inheritance is not a general vindication of the described historical claims.

rows.passage_en: Under incomplete dominance, a heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype. Crossing two such heterozygotes gives a one-to-two-to-one genotype ratio, with the intermediate phenotype in roughly half the offspring.
rows.review_note: Counts8white17gray7black fit1:2:1. The accessed glossary only gives synonym partial dominance, not the full mechanism: final source support needs a fuller genetics passage. Codominance would express distinguishable parental traits rather than an intermediate gray phenotype.

rows.source_locator: ATP synthase figure and membrane components
rows.passage_en: ATP synthase uses the electrochemical gradient of protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Protons flowing through the enzyme toward the matrix supply the immediate energy for ATP synthesis.
rows.review_note: Electron transfer builds the gradient upstream; the question asks immediate energy source. Source figure explicitly shows direction and membrane machinery.

rows.passage_en: Trypsin is a protein enzyme that catalyzes peptide-bond hydrolysis. Its activity depends on conditions including pH; its optimum is near pH eight rather than equally strong activity across arbitrary acidic and alkaline conditions.
rows.review_note: Manufacturer bulletin explicitly identifies enzyme, cleavage activity and near8optimum; no claim numerical range endpoints not provided. Wide is vague; final review should inspect pH-activity profile rather than infer narrowness from optimum alone.

rows.source_locator: Anatomy, Autonomic Nervous System, sympathetic effects
rows.passage_en: Sympathetic activation generally inhibits gastrointestinal peristalsis while supporting fight-or-flight responses such as pupil dilation and sweating. Parasympathetic activity generally promotes digestive motility.
rows.review_note: Exact indexed source explicitly says inhibition of gastrointestinal peristalsis; full page blocked. Vascular responses differ across tissues; do not imply uniform constriction of every vessel.

rows.source_locator: genomic change and common ancestry background
rows.passage_en: Similarity in many corresponding DNA sequences and proteins can provide evidence of close evolutionary relationship. Close common ancestry makes inherited structural similarity more plausible than an explanation based only on similar environmental demands.
rows.review_note: General NHGRI evolution page accessed but does not directly establish molecular homology testing; needs a specific comparative-sequence source before final approval. Similar function alone cannot decide homology.

Intended A for bacterial F-type ATP synthase, but the prompt calls the machinery generically proton pumps (ATPases). Plant and fungal plasma membranes also have proton-pumping ATPases, so D can be true under literal wording. Need distinguish enzyme family/direction or replace; do not edit the published stem.

rows.source_locator: Fates of Pyruvic Acid, fermentation equations
rows.passage_en: Fermentation oxidizes NADH back to NAD+ while reducing an organic intermediate. This replenishes NAD+ for glycolysis when aerobic electron transport cannot do so.
rows.review_note: Prompt uses respiration loosely; fermentation permits glycolysis, not continued oxygen-dependent oxidative phosphorylation. Source explicitly shows NAD+ products in lactate and ethanol fermentation.

rows.passage_en: Across a membrane that passes water but retains the dissolved solute, water moves toward the side with higher solute concentration. A solute-filled bag placed in pure water therefore tends to take in water and swell.
rows.review_note: Requires membrane retention of the relevant solute; dialysis membrane permeability is not universal for all solutes. Standard question assumes a retained solute; final language review must preserve that conditional scope.

rows.passage_en: Pioneer organisms can alter a newly colonized environment, for example by changing substrate or adding organic matter. Under the facilitation model, those changes make establishment easier for later species.
rows.review_note: The source explicitly distinguishes facilitation from tolerance/inhibition. Question generalizes to all pioneers; review whether best-option educational reading is acceptable or replace to avoid a model-specific assertion.

rows.passage_en: A pesticide can favor insects that already carry heritable resistance variants. Their greater survival and reproduction can increase the frequency of resistance over generations.
rows.review_note: Indexed Khan explanation explicitly describes pre-existing DDT alleles, but the exact1959India history and “all susceptible exterminated” wording need verification. Do not claim every susceptible mosquito must die or that resistance cannot ever involve a new mutation.

rows.passage_en: A Barr body is a compact, largely inactive X chromosome. This condensed, relatively transcriptionally silent chromatin is an example of facultative heterochromatin.
rows.review_note: Kimball compact/inactive description accessed; explicit heterochromatin term confirmed in indexed Cooper NBK10075 excerpt. Not all X-linked genes are fully silenced.

rows.passage_en: Tracheids and vessel elements are water-conducting xylem cells. Their reinforced walls also contribute structural support, and they are dead at functional maturity.
rows.review_note: Source distinguishes xylem conducting cells from phloem sieve tubes and companion cells; concise factual paraphrase, no copied textbook passage.

rows.passage_en: When striated muscle is inactive, tropomyosin blocks myosin interaction with binding sites on actin. Calcium binding to troponin shifts tropomyosin and allows cross-bridge formation.
rows.review_note: Direct relevant source paragraphs read. Myosin heads, not helical tails, have actin-binding and ATPase sites.

rows.source_locator: section3.1 Cell Types and Cell Characteristics, page164
rows.passage_en: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes and lack a membrane-enclosed nucleus. Green unicellular algae are eukaryotes with nuclei and other membrane-enclosed organelles.
rows.review_note: WHO authored chapter explicitly states cyanobacteria lack a cell nucleus and chloroplasts; relevant paragraph read. Conventional comparison with green unicellular eukaryotic algae.

rows.source_locator: stem ground tissue and pith rays
rows.passage_en: Parenchyma are living ground-tissue cells used in storage and other basic plant functions. The central pith of a typical dicot stem is primarily parenchyma.
rows.review_note: Accessed Kimball page explicitly identifies pith rays as parenchyma, not all central pith text. Final check needs central-pith statement or original diagram legend; background source alone is not exact direct verification.

rows.source_locator: proton flow through mitochondrial ATP synthase
rows.passage_en: The mitochondrial outer membrane permits small solutes to equilibrate relatively readily. Acidifying the outside can increase intermembrane-space proton concentration, so a gradient toward a less acidic matrix can drive ATP synthase.
rows.review_note: Source confirms matrix-directed proton flow; outer-membrane permeability and the experimental low-pH setup need a direct additional source before approval. Assumes intact inner membrane, sufficient ADP/Pi and transient maintained gradient.

rows.passage_en: Fungal cell walls commonly contain chitin, a structural polysaccharide made from N-acetylglucosamine units. Chitin contributes rigidity and reinforcement.
rows.review_note: Author textbook relevant passage available in indexed full excerpt; final full-page/reuse check pending. Fungal walls also contain glucans and other components, not chitin alone.

rows.passage_en: Reducing leaf area and using spines can limit transpiration in dry environments. Spines may also shade the surface and reduce local airflow, helping reduce water loss.
rows.review_note: Botanic Gardens of Sydney indexed author explanation accessed; full page timed out. Kew Cacti Characteristics PDF independently corroborates water-loss effects.

Thrombin is not a typical constituent listed for solid connective tissue, but blood is classified as connective tissue and thrombin can be present during coagulation. Wording “might be found in connective tissue” is too broad to exclude it unconditionally. Needs histology-specific adjudication or replacement; cited glossary only illustrates blood proteins, not proof of key.

rows.source_locator: Hardy-Weinberg law and changes in gene pool
rows.passage_en: In population genetics, evolutionary change is tracked as changes in allele frequencies across generations. A population maintaining the same allele frequencies across generations does not show that kind of evolutionary change.
rows.review_note: This is allele-frequency definition in question, not a claim that all possible higher-level evolutionary concepts reduce to the measured finite loci. Distinguish population gene pool from a single individual genotype.

rows.source_locator: When the Hardy-Weinberg Law Fails: Genetic Drift
rows.passage_en: The ideal Hardy-Weinberg model assumes random mating and no changes from mutation, migration, selection, or appreciable genetic drift. A very large population reduces random sampling changes in allele frequency.
rows.review_note: Source explicitly lists drift as a failure condition and describes small populations. HW genotype equilibrium and constancy of allele frequencies are distinct related assumptions.

rows.source_locator: Cellular Level: Smooth Muscle, IP3 paragraph
rows.passage_en: Inositol trisphosphate, IP3, binds intracellular calcium-release channels on the endoplasmic or sarcoplasmic reticulum. This releases stored calcium into the cytoplasm.
rows.review_note: Direct paragraph read in muscle physiology source; IP3 is the signal opening release channels, while calmodulin binds calcium downstream.

rows.source_locator: vessel elements and tracheids at maturity
rows.passage_en: Water-conducting vessel elements undergo programmed cell death during maturation, leaving hollow, reinforced conduits. Functional sieve-tube members instead remain living despite losing their nuclei.
rows.review_note: Source directly states dead maturity of vessels/tracheids. Programmed mechanism and live sieve element contrast need corresponding maturation passages before final approval.

rows.source_locator: three membrane types and imported proteins
rows.passage_en: A protein starting in the cytosol must cross a chloroplast’s outer and inner envelope membranes to enter the stroma. To reach the thylakoid lumen, it must additionally cross the thylakoid membrane.
rows.review_note: Independent membrane count:2envelope+1thylakoid=3. Nuclear transcription does not add a membrane crossing for the protein, because the protein is synthesized in cytoplasm. Counts bilayers, not lipid leaflets.

rows.passage_en: Colchicine binds tubulin and disrupts microtubules, including the mitotic spindle. Interfering with chromosome segregation after DNA replication can produce cells with additional chromosome sets.
rows.review_note: FDA primary review confirms tubulin/spindle and mitotic arrest. The polyploidization consequence needs a direct experimental/botanical citation in final review; it is not guaranteed for every treated cell.

rows.source_locator: History of Discovery: The LDL Receptor
rows.passage_en: LDL binds a cell-surface receptor and is internalized through coated pits into endocytic vesicles and endosomes. Adhesion plaques are structures for attachment, not required components of the standard LDL uptake pathway.
rows.review_note: Author-history indexed passage describes their own LDL receptor experiments and receptor recycling. Full article access and adhesion-plaque contrast pending; no medical recommendation.

rows.passage_en: The src gene encodes a protein tyrosine kinase. This enzyme transfers phosphate groups to tyrosine residues in target proteins rather than removing phosphate groups.
rows.review_note: Reviewed UniProt indexed record read; browser returns JavaScript-only shell. Exact v-src oncogene versus cellular proto-oncogene distinction needs care, but both encode tyrosine kinases.

rows.source_locator: table of suggested successional ecosystem changes, after Odum1969
rows.passage_en: The classical ecosystem-development model predicts a high ratio of gross primary production to standing biomass early in succession, with less accumulated organic matter than in later stages.
rows.review_note: Table directly checked. Label explicitly as classical prediction, not universal empirical law; modern succession depends on disturbance and site. Primary Odum1969 table should replace course reproduction as final reference.

rows.passage_en: A monoclonal antibody preparation traces to a single antibody-producing cell clone and has much less antibody diversity than a polyclonal preparation, which derives from multiple B-cell lineages.
rows.review_note: IUPAC indexed definition explicitly compares diversity; full page403. NCI andNHGRI establish antibodies andBcells but not lineage contrast; final primary-definition paragraph needed. Antibodies are not secreted by Tcells.

rows.passage_en: The familiar fern plant is the dominant diploid sporophyte. It produces haploid spores by meiosis; these grow into smaller, independent gametophytes that produce gametes by mitosis.
rows.review_note: Direct author textbook paragraphs read; sporophyte embryo initially depends on gametophyte before becoming self-supporting. No equal-life-span assumption.

rows.passage_en: Retrotransposons copy through an RNA intermediate. Their RNA is reverse-transcribed into DNA, which can be inserted into a new genomic position.
rows.review_note: Researcher presentation directly read including mechanism diagram. Distinguishes copy-and-paste retrotransposition from DNA cut-and-paste transposition.

Intended archaeon, but “isoprenylglycerol ethers instead of phospholipids” confuses ether linkages with phosphate headgroups: archaeal membrane lipids can themselves be phospholipids. The supplied characters still point to archaea, but factual premise needs correction; published question cannot be silently edited. Seek explicit membrane-lipid definition before final exclusion.

rows.source_locator: air composition and dissolved oxygen solubility
rows.passage_en: Under ordinary environmental conditions, oxygen gas is much more abundant per unit volume in air than dissolved oxygen is in water. Water is denser, provides greater buoyant support, and resists movement more strongly.
rows.review_note: Do not confuse oxygen atoms bound in H2O with dissolved O2 usable for respiration. Source gives air20.9%andwatermL/L; exact unit conversions independently derived. Unusual pressurized or supersaturated water outside intended setting.

rows.passage_en: Water moves into a cell or grain when the surrounding solution has lower effective solute concentration than its interior. That inward osmotic flow can swell and rupture the structure rather than shrink it.
rows.review_note: Given hypothesized osmotic rupture, interior has higher effective osmotic pressure. This deduction does not establish the historical thunderstorm-asthma theory or validate the prompt’s five-micrometer threshold.
